title: When a dying person seems to know, say, or gesture that the end is near

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source utterance/listening-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe communication patterns and response guidance but do not supply consented verbatim bedside testimony.
This record must not become a prophecy, last-words trope, spiritual proof, diagnosis, countdown, or mandatory script.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and safety decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: A person says they are going soon, the end is near, someone is coming, or gives a timing-like statement; family and staff may wonder whether the person knows something, is afraid, is lucid, or is confused.
ordinary_language_queries: dying person says the end is near
hospice patient knows when death will happen

content_layers.observation_text: This record preserves timing-like statements while building a hard nonprophecy boundary: the archive may record that such statements are made, but cannot treat them as reliable prediction engines.
content_layers.source_synthesis: PCNOW lists knowing when death will occur among NDA content, while Virtual Hospice treats death-related cues as openings for listening; the peer-reviewed last-words source warns that interactional data are sparse and context matters.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: Utterance records should preserve what was heard, who heard it, and what interpretive frames were available without deciding meaning for the family or turning speech into a rule.

what_this_is_not: not proof the person controls timing
not a replacement for clinical assessment
uncertainties: Need stronger literature review and consented examples.
Statements may be metaphor, fear, planning, delirium, NDA, or ordinary awareness of decline.
Family memory may sharpen after the death.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should say the statement may be meaningful and worth listening to, but it is not a dependable clock. Urgent care concerns still go to the care team.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect how the statement was received, whether the person wanted to talk more, and whether distress, delirium, pain, breathlessness, or spiritual concern was present.
language_notes: Never route search queries to exact time estimates.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the utterance layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, not proof of spiritual meaning, not a diagnosis of delirium, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent distress, safety, medication, confusion, swallowing, legal, or crisis concerns to qualified local support.
